items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: He called me and said, 'How would you like to be on the staff at of Columbia Studios? They want you on the staff.'

ctx.x: But during the meantime when Stan really thought I was gonna join the band, and I had said I was gonna join the

band, but Dave Klein, who was the biggest contractor in town at the time, was Manny Klein's brother. He called me and said, 'How would you like to be on the staff at of Columbia Studios? They want you on the staff.' And I told him that I had this commitment with Stan, and I really wanted to go with the band, but I didn't want to leave home, but I wanted to play with the band, you know.

And, Davis was really one of the nicest men, and I think he did more for musicians than -- and helped musicians in more ways than he was probably ever given credit for. Now he talked to me like a father, you know. He explained to me how important this was for me to do this, you know; as a contractor, he said that he had tried to get black musicians on gigs and he had been turned down. And he knew that I could cut it, and I had to take the job because it would be others following me that I would set a good example…
